previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant status, and recent loss of her father was admitted for leg swelling and malaise following a urinary tract infection. She had gained 7 pounds despite self-administering old Lasix tablets. Evaluation showed no acute cardiopulmonary process, no DVT, and stable kidney function. Her white count initially rose but improved, and blood cultures were negative. CMV was not detected, and EBV testing indicated past but not active infection. She was continued on cefpodoxime for the UTI and started on a scheduled regimen of furosemide every other day. Her symptoms improved during the admission, and she was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue antibiotics, and follow up with her transplant team and weekly labs.

FINDINGS: 

The left iliac fossa transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically, the
cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there is
no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal.  There is no
hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.76 to 0.88,
previously ranging from 0.81 to 0.87 on ___.  The main renal artery
shows a normal waveform, with prompt systolic upstroke and continuous
antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity of 96.7 cm/sec.
Vascularity is symmetric throughout the transplant. The transplant renal vein
is patent and shows normal waveform.
